title: dissectors: add Ultra Ethernet Transport
description:
The specification is available from ultraethernet.org (currently version
1.0.1 [1]).  This dissector covers the UE Transport layer (chapter 3)
protocols, which sit on top of IP or UDP.

[1] https://ultraethernet.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2025/10/UE-Specification-1.0.1.pdf

Co-authored-by: Manomugdha Biswas <manomugdha.biswas@keysight.com>
Co-authored-by: Evan Green <evan@rivosinc.com>
Co-authored-by: Daniel Verkamp <drv@rivosinc.com>
Co-authored-by: Alex Badea <alex.badea@keysight.com>

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22094/diffs?diff_id=1544110322&start_sha=5a8a8d3711c798f3d261d241479d33c7d20e0d6d#7ff0044177febc6ffdca031c20cba3b4fd66c77b_40_21)

These should be converted to proto_tree_add_item with the hf_ value including the bitmask necessary.
(This is probably true of all proto_tree_add_bits_items in this dissector)
Is this another copy/paste idea from another dissector?  Why would you want to turn this on/off? (Presuming it would just always be on)
As in, the summary_in_tree pref? Good question, I'll ask.
I didn't get a straight answer.  Would you like me to remove the pref and consider it always `true`?
Yes

changed this line in [version 7 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22094/diffs?diff_id=1598975390&start_sha=e4680a4ce3c8c5ff41fc7deca3f4c4f8d6e29b14#7ff0044177febc6ffdca031c20cba3b4fd66c77b_2641_2615)
If the size is too small, won't this lead to a malformed packet if you don't return here?  Is that desired?
(as below) it would, but some may dissect a few of the fields, which can still be useful.  Let me know if you'd like to make it return instead.
Look at proto_tree_add_bitmask for cleaner ways to handle this

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22094/diffs?diff_id=1545529714&start_sha=84371bceac8c8bb1a033d41e70f5badb57872c66#7ff0044177febc6ffdca031c20cba3b4fd66c77b_1458_1367)
proto_tree_add_bitmask (and similarly named APIs) should help here.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22094/diffs?diff_id=1545529714&start_sha=84371bceac8c8bb1a033d41e70f5badb57872c66#7ff0044177febc6ffdca031c20cba3b4fd66c77b_1183_1133)
Will this just lead to a malformed packet?
Well yes, eventually.  But it might dissect a few of the fields, maybe that is still helpful?  Not sure what's typical -- exit early, or try our best.

Given that this has an identical length and mask as rsv3, do you really need separate filters to distinguish these, or would a single item suffice?

Also hf_uet_ses_small_req_rsv3 and hf_uet_ses_small_req_rsv4 - should they all just use the same field?

Not sure.  Having them separate like this would allow filtering on them separately; that could be useful with buggy implementations or not-yet-handled future extensions.

I can unify them if that's uncommon, let me know.
We can leave them as separate if you wish.
